title: Symmetrical Components & Unbalanced Faults
description: The operator a, positive-, negative- and zero-sequence components, sequence networks, transformer grounding and the currents of line-to-ground, line-to-line and double line-to-ground faults.

study.title: Symmetrical components
study.body: Any set of three unbalanced phasors can be written as the sum of three **balanced** sets (Fortescue): a **positive-sequence** set (abc order, like normal operation), a **negative-sequence** set (acb order) and a **zero-sequence** set (three equal phasors in phase). The operator $a = 1\angle120°$ rotates a phasor by 120°; note $a^2 = 1\angle240°$ and $1 + a + a^2 = 0$.
study.formula: \begin{aligned}V_a &= V_0 + V_1 + V_2\\ V_b &= V_0 + a^2V_1 + aV_2\\ V_c &= V_0 + aV_1 + a^2V_2\end{aligned}

study.title: Finding the components
study.body: Inverting the relations above gives the sequence components of phase a (those of b and c follow by rotation). The zero-sequence current is a third of the **neutral** current, $I_n = I_a + I_b + I_c = 3I_0$: without a neutral or ground path there is no zero-sequence current.
study.formula: \begin{aligned}V_0 &= \tfrac13(V_a + V_b + V_c)\\ V_1 &= \tfrac13(V_a + aV_b + a^2V_c)\\ V_2 &= \tfrac13(V_a + a^2V_b + aV_c)\end{aligned}

study.title: Explore: building an unbalanced set
study.body: A positive-sequence set of 1.0 pu plus an adjustable negative-sequence $V_2$ and zero-sequence $V_0$ (in phase with the real axis). With only $V_1$ the three phasors are balanced on the unit circle. A negative-sequence component makes the magnitudes unequal and the angles no longer 120° apart; a zero-sequence component shifts all three by the same phasor.

study.title: Sequence networks
Transformer zero-sequence paths
study.body:
Zero-sequence currents are three equal in-phase currents; they need a neutral connection to flow.
- **Yg–Yg**: passes zero-sequence current from one side to the other (series $Z_0$).
- **Yg–Δ**: the in-phase currents circulate inside the delta, so the grounded-Y side sees a path to ground through $Z_0$, while the delta side is **open**.
- **ungrounded Y** or **Δ–Δ**: open on both sides.
A grounding impedance $Z_n$ in a Y neutral appears as $3Z_n$, because all three phase currents pass through it. (Y–Δ units also shift positive-sequence quantities by ±30° and negative-sequence by ∓30°.)

study.title: Single line-to-ground fault
study.body: Phase a to ground through $Z_F$: $I_b = I_c = 0$ forces $I_0 = I_1 = I_2$, so the three sequence networks (Thévenin impedances at the fault, $Z_1$, $Z_2$, $Z_0$) are connected **in series** with $3Z_F$. The fault current is $3I_0$. With $Z_2 = Z_1$ it exceeds the three-phase fault current when $Z_0 < Z_1$, e.g. at a solidly grounded generator.

study.title: Line-to-line and double line-to-ground faults
study.body: **Line-to-line** (b to c through $Z_F$): no ground involved, so $I_0 = 0$; positive and negative networks in parallel-opposition: $I_1 = -I_2$, and $I_b = -I_c = -j\sqrt3\,I_1$. **Double line-to-ground** (b and c to ground): all three networks in **parallel** at the fault; the ground current is $3I_0$.
study.formula: \begin{aligned}\text{LL: } I_1 &= \frac{V_F}{Z_1 + Z_2 + Z_F}\\ \text{DLG: } I_1 &= \frac{V_F}{Z_1 + Z_2\parallel(Z_0 + 3Z_F)}\\ I_0 &= -I_1\frac{Z_2}{Z_2 + Z_0 + 3Z_F}\end{aligned}

study.title: Worked example: four fault types

lessons.title: The operator a and sequence components

steps.title: Three balanced sets
steps.body: Any unbalanced set of three phasors is the sum of a **positive-sequence** set (abc), a **negative-sequence** set (acb) and a **zero-sequence** set (all in phase). The operator $a = 1\angle120° = -0.5 + j0.866$ rotates by 120°:
steps.formula: \begin{aligned}V_a &= V_0 + V_1 + V_2\\ V_b &= V_0 + a^2V_1 + aV_2\\ V_c &= V_0 + aV_1 + a^2V_2\end{aligned}

steps.prompt: What is $a^2$?
steps.explanation: Rotating twice by 120° gives 240° (the same as −120°): $a^2 = -0.5 - j0.866$. Then $1 + a + a^2$ = 1 − 0.5 − 0.5 + j(0.866 − 0.866) = 0, the identity used throughout.

steps.prompt: A balanced positive-sequence set has $V_a$ = {{V|V}}∠0° and $V_b = a^2V_a$. Find $|V_a - V_b|$, the line-to-line voltage.

steps.title: Finding the components
steps.body: Inverting the relations gives the sequence components. The zero-sequence current is a third of the neutral current.
steps.formula: \begin{aligned}I_0 &= \tfrac13(I_a + I_b + I_c)\\ I_1 &= \tfrac13(I_a + aI_b + a^2I_c)\\ I_2 &= \tfrac13(I_a + a^2I_b + aI_c)\end{aligned}

steps.prompt: The phase currents are $I_a$ = {{A}}∠0°, $I_b$ = {{B}}∠−120° and $I_c$ = {{C}}∠120° A: 120° apart, but with unequal magnitudes.

steps.title: Explore: an unbalanced set
steps.body: A 1.0-pu positive-sequence set plus a negative-sequence component $V_2$ and a zero-sequence component $V_0$. Watch the magnitudes become unequal.

steps.prompt: A balanced set in abc order has no negative- or zero-sequence components.
Phase c of a grounded-wye load is disconnected, leaving $I_a$ = {{A}}∠0° A, $I_b$ = {{B}}∠−120° A and $I_c$ = 0. Find the neutral current.
Match each sequence to its description.
steps.explanation: Positive sequence is the normal balanced set; negative sequence rotates the other way and induces double-frequency currents in machine rotors; zero sequence is in phase in all three phases and returns through the neutral or ground as $3I_0$.

steps.title: Sequence networks
steps.body: Balanced equipment does not mix sequences, so each sequence has its own per-phase network. Only the **positive** network contains the generator EMFs. A neutral grounding impedance $Z_n$ carries $3I_0$, so it appears as $3Z_n$ in the zero-sequence network.

steps.prompt: A generator's neutral is grounded through a reactance $X_n$. How does it appear in the generator's sequence networks?
options: As $3X_n$ in the zero-sequence network only
steps.explanation: Positive- and negative-sequence currents sum to zero in the neutral, so $X_n$ carries no current for them. The three zero-sequence currents all flow through it: the voltage $3I_0X_n$ per phase means an impedance of $3X_n$ in the zero-sequence network.

steps.prompt: A 100-MVA, 13.8-kV generator has $X_{g0}$ = {{Xg0}} pu and its neutral is grounded through {{Xn}} Ω. Find its total zero-sequence reactance in per unit (100-MVA, 13.8-kV base).

steps.title: Transformer zero-sequence paths
steps.body:
- **Yg–Yg**: zero-sequence current passes through (series $Z_0$).
- **Yg–Δ**: path to ground on the Y side (the currents circulate in the delta); the Δ side is open.
- **Δ–Δ** or ungrounded Y: open, no zero-sequence current in the lines.
Positive- and negative-sequence currents pass through all of them.

steps.prompt: Match each transformer connection to its zero-sequence behaviour seen from the lines.
pairs: Passes $I_0$ through to the other side
Ground path on the Y side only
No zero-sequence path on either side
steps.explanation: A delta winding lets in-phase currents circulate inside it but offers no neutral to the lines. A grounded wye provides a neutral; it can pass $I_0$ to the other side only if that side also has a grounded neutral.

steps.prompt: During a ground fault on the grounded-Y side of a Yg–Δ transformer, zero-sequence current flows in its Y windings although none flows in the lines on the Δ side.
steps.explanation: The zero-sequence currents in the Y windings induce in-phase currents in the three delta windings, which simply circulate around the delta. The line currents on the delta side are differences of winding currents, so their zero-sequence part cancels.

steps.title: Single line-to-ground fault
steps.body: For phase a to ground through $Z_F$, $I_b = I_c = 0$ gives $I_0 = I_1 = I_2$: the three sequence networks (Thévenin impedances $Z_1$, $Z_2$, $Z_0$ at the fault) are in **series**.

steps.prompt: At a bus, $Z_1$ = j{{X1}}, $Z_2$ = j{{X2}} and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu. Find the current of a bolted single line-to-ground fault ($V_F$ = 1.0 pu).
steps.explanation: $I_0$ = $1/[j({{X1}} + {{X2}} + {{X0}})]$ = −j{{1/(X1+X2+X0)}} pu, and $I_a = 3I_0$, magnitude {{3/(X1 + X2 + X0)|pu}}. A three-phase fault would give 1/{{X1}} = {{1/X1}} pu.

steps.title: Line-to-line and double line-to-ground
steps.body: **LL** (b–c): no zero sequence; $I_1 = -I_2 = V_F/(Z_1 + Z_2 + Z_F)$ and $|I_b| = \sqrt3|I_1|$. **DLG** (b and c to ground): the three networks are in parallel at the fault, and the ground current is $3I_0$.

steps.prompt: Find the fault current of a bolted line-to-line fault at a bus with $Z_1$ = j{{X1}} and $Z_2$ = j{{X2}} pu ($V_F$ = 1.0 pu).
At a {{V|V}} bus (100-MVA base), $Z_1 = Z_2$ = j{{X1}} pu and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu. Find the current of a bolted single line-to-ground fault.
At a {{V|V}} bus (100-MVA base), $Z_1 = Z_2$ = j{{X1}} pu. Find the current of a bolted line-to-line fault.
steps.explanation: $|I_b| = \sqrt3/(Z_1 + Z_2)$ = 1.732/{{2*X1}} = {{sqrt(3)/(2*X1)}} pu, i.e. 0.866 times the three-phase value. In amperes: × {{1e8/(sqrt(3)*V)|A}} = {{sqrt(3)/(2*X1)*1e8/(sqrt(3)*V)|A}}.

steps.prompt: A bolted double line-to-ground fault (b and c to ground) occurs at a bus with $Z_1$ = j{{X1}}, $Z_2$ = j{{X2}} and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu. Find the current flowing into the ground.
At a bus with $Z_1 = Z_2$ = j{{X1}} pu and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu, which bolted fault draws the larger current from phase a?
steps.explanation: Three-phase: 1/{{X1}} = {{1/X1}} pu. Line-to-ground: 3/(2 × {{X1}} + {{X0}}) = {{3/(2*X1 + X0)}} pu. The ground fault is larger exactly when $Z_0 < Z_1$, typical at the terminals of solidly grounded generators and at Yg–Δ transformers.

steps.prompt: A line-to-ground fault through an arc resistance $R_F$ = {{RF}} pu occurs at a bus with $Z_1 = Z_2$ = j{{X1}} and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu. Find the magnitude of the fault current.
A bolted line-to-ground fault on phase a occurs at a bus with $Z_1 = Z_2$ = j{{X1}} and $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu ($V_F$ = 1.0 pu). Find the magnitude of the voltage of the healthy phase b during the fault.
A line-to-line fault produces no zero-sequence current.
steps.explanation: Ground is not involved: $I_a = 0$ and $I_b = -I_c$, so $I_a + I_b + I_c = 0 = 3I_0$. Only the positive- and negative-sequence networks take part, connected in parallel-opposition ($I_1 = -I_2$).

steps.prompt: A 100-MVA, 13.8-kV generator has $X_1 = X_2$ = {{X1}} pu and $X_{g0}$ = {{X0}} pu (own base). What neutral grounding reactance, in ohms, limits its terminal line-to-ground fault current to the three-phase value?
Measured phase voltages: $V_a$ = {{Va}}∠0°, $V_b$ = {{Vb}}∠{{tb}}° and $V_c$ = {{Vc}}∠{{tc}}° pu.

ask.prompt: Find the negative-sequence voltage $|V_2|$ in per unit.
ask.explanation: $a^2V_b$ = {{Vb}}∠{{tb + 240}}° and $aV_c$ = {{Vc}}∠{{tc + 120}}°. $V_2 = (V_a + a^2V_b + aV_c)/3$ = {{v2r||3}} + j({{v2i||3}}), so $|V_2|$ = {{sqrt(v2r^2 + v2i^2)||3}} pu. The three terms nearly cancel, so carry four decimals. ($|V_1|$, by contrast, is almost exactly the average of the three magnitudes when the unbalance is small.)

ask.prompt: Find the voltage unbalance factor $|V_2|/|V_1|$ in per cent.

steps.prompt: A bolted double line-to-ground fault (phases b and c) occurs at a bus with $Z_1$ = j{{X1}}, $Z_2$ = j{{X2}}, $Z_0$ = j{{X0}} pu. Find $|I_b|$.
Which phasor diagram shows a **negative-sequence** set?
steps.explanation: In a negative-sequence set the phasors are equal and 120° apart, but in acb order: $V_b$ **leads** $V_a$ by 120° ($V_b = aV_a$) and $V_c$ lags by 120°. The abc set ($V_b$ lagging $V_a$ by 120°) is positive sequence, and phasors that are not 120° apart form an unbalanced set containing several sequences.

steps.prompt: A generator ($X'' = X_2$ = {{Xg}} pu, any $X_0$) feeds a {{V|V}} line through a Δ–Yg step-up transformer (Δ on the generator side, Yg on the line side, $X_T$ = {{XT}} pu). The line has $X_1$ = {{XL1}} pu and $X_0$ = {{k0*XL1}} pu (100-MVA base). Find the current of a bolted line-to-ground fault at the far end of the line.
steps.explanation: $Z_1 = Z_2$ = {{Xg}} + {{XT}} + {{XL1}} = {{Z1}} pu. Zero sequence: the delta isolates the generator, and the Yg winding gives a path to ground through $X_T$, so $Z_0$ = {{XT}} + {{k0*XL1}} = {{Z0}} pu. $I_a = 3/(2Z_1 + Z_0)$ = {{3/(2*Z1 + Z0)}} pu × {{1e8/(sqrt(3)*V)|A}} = {{3/(2*Z1 + Z0)*1e8/(sqrt(3)*V)|A}}.

steps.prompt: Put the steps for computing a single line-to-ground fault current in order.
items: Build the positive-, negative- and zero-sequence networks
Find $Z_1$, $Z_2$ and $Z_0$ seen from the fault bus
Connect the three networks in series with $3Z_F$
steps.explanation: The sequence networks come first (with each transformer's zero-sequence connection), then their Thévenin impedances at the fault. The fault's boundary conditions decide how they connect; for a line-to-ground fault they are in series.
